transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Owen (Redwood SE), Elena (Venturi CISO), Samir (Venturi Platform), Priya (Legal), Tom (SRE)
Shared files: security-deck-v2.pdf, private-deploy-sample.tf, redwood-kms-integration-notes.md

Summary (autogenerated, may be rough): 
Quick security posture intake for Venturi evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on encryption/KMS key custody, SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and audit logging retention. Customer wants private key custody and data residency options; legal asks about contractual retention controls and pen test evidence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see the Venturi crew and a few of our engs, so we can do an intake for the security and deployment questions. Quick round-robin to confirm roles?
[00:12] Elena: Elena Ruiz, CISO. I'm here to assess controls and make sure any vendor meets our compliance baseline.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, platform engineering — I'll be the primary technical owner.
[00:21] Priya: Priya, legal — contracts and data retention side.
[00:24] Tom: Tom, SRE, ops and runbook questions.
[00:28] Jesse: Cool. From Redwood, I'm Jesse (AE), Maya (SE) and Owen from solutions. We'll run through SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS and retention. 
[00:38] [crosstalk]
[00:40] Maya: Quick note — we have three main deployment options that impact the security posture: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for you) and Private (VPC/on-prem with customer managed control plane). We'll map each to your controls.
[00:54] Elena: We generally require SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Do you have those now?
[00:59] Jesse: Yes — we maintain SOC2 Type II and are ISO 27001 certified. I'll send the latest attestation binder after the call. There's a public summary in the security-deck-v2.pdf and we can provide the AICPA report under NDA.
[01:12] Priya: What's the date range on the SOC2 report? We need the period covered.
[01:15] Jesse: The most recent covers Jan through Oct 2027. I'll include exact dates in the email.
[01:19] Samir: On encryption — we need to understand key custody. For HIPAA-esque workloads we prefer customer-managed keys. Does Redwood support CMEK?
[01:28] Owen: Yes — for Private deployments you can bring your own keys (BYOK) integrated with major cloud KMS providers. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration with customer-managed keys in many cases; Hosted has envelope encryption and we support customer master key options for enterprise seats. There's nuance across clouds and HSM support.
[01:45] Tom: OK, does that mean keys can live in our KMS/HSM? We want cryptographic separation where root keys never touch Redwood-managed HSM.
[01:52] Maya: For Private (VPC/on-prem) you can manage the KMS/HSM entirely — Redwood's control plane can be configured to never have raw key material. For Dedicated we can configure CMEK where you control the CMKs in your cloud account and Redwood uses KMS API calls to decrypt per-request. I should flag that some hardware-backed attestation flows require additional setup but it's supported.
[02:10] Elena: Audit logs — how long are API and access logs retained? We also need immutable audit trails for user actions (SSO logins, API key usage).
[02:19] Jesse: By default Hosted retains logs for 90 days; Dedicated can be configured to push logs to your logging endpoint (S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery) and set retention on your side. Private gives you direct control and we can ship logs to your SIEM in near real time.
[02:32] Priya: For contract language, we need to be able to specify retention windows and deletion proof for data in the contract. How do you handle data deletion?
[02:41] Owen: We have data deletion APIs and a documented deletion workflow; for Private and Dedicated you can enforce retention controls yourself. For Hosted, we provide deletion and can produce deletion certificates for the covered data plane under specific SLA and contractual terms — we'll include scope details in the binder.
[02:55] Samir: A technical question — does Redwood store KV cache or prefix cache on disk? Is that encrypted? If we serve long contexts we need to ensure cache TTL and purge are controllable.
[03:05] Maya: Good callout. Runtime caches (KV/prefix) are in memory by default for latency; if spill-to-disk is enabled in certain configurations we encrypt at rest. For Dedicated/Private you can require in-memory-only or ensure storage is encrypted with your CMK. We'll add a note to the architecture doc.
[03:23] [pause]
[03:27] Elena: SSO — we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning, plus SSO audit logs feeding into our IDP. Do you support SAML + SCIM? MFA? RBAC granularity?
[03:38] Jesse: Yes — we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for syncing groups. RBAC is role-based with team and token scopes; we support custom roles for enterprise via the console or API. MFA is enforced at the IDP level; we can require device-binding via SAML assertions.
[03:51] Priya: For legal, we need to confirm single-tenant VLAN segregation for Dedicated or Private. Also, any sub processors?
[03:59] Owen: Dedicated gives you logical separation; Private is single-tenant. Our subprocessor list is in the security binder — we'll provide the latest vendor list. Contracts can include restrictions on subprocessors and notification timelines for changes.
[04:14] Tom: Pen tests and vuln scanning — do you do external pen tests regularly and will you share summary reports or remediation trackers?
[04:22] Maya: We run annual 3rd-party pen tests and regular internal scans. We can share executive summaries and remediation timelines under NDA. For Dedicated/private we can coordinate additional testing in some cases.
[04:34] Samir: What about model artifacts and provenance — we have IP concerns around embeddings and transcripts. If we send PII into hosted, does Redwood retain transiently for caching or training?
[04:44] Jesse: We do not train models on customer data; default is no customer data used for training. For Hosted, we have a configurable data retention policy and can turn off telemetry or caching of content to meet privacy needs. For Dedicated/Private, data stays in your environment. We'll capture this in the compliance sheet.
[05:02] Elena: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for some customers. Are there region restrictions and guaranteed residency?
[05:08] Owen: Yes — we have region routing policies. For Hosted we can pin to EU regions for data processing; Dedicated in a specific region is supported and Private obviously can be deployed in your on-prem or regional VPC. We'll include a region availability matrix.
[05:18] [short gap]
[05:22] Priya: Contractual question — are you willing to include SOC2 carve-outs (controls mapping) in the MSA?
[05:28] Jesse: We've worked with enterprise legal teams to map controls; we can provide a control matrix and work through carve-outs. We'll ask legal to take the lead on a controls mapping session.
[05:36] Tom: Monitoring and alerting — do you provide audit hooks for token-level usage, per-route latency and cost breakdowns? Our SREs want to hook into tracing and be able to alert on anomalous token spikes.
[05:48] Maya: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level usage, per-model per-route metrics, traces and logs. For Dedicated/Private you can route traces to your tracing backend. We also have alerting webhooks.
[05:58] Samir: Licensing — if we go Dedicated, what's the upgrade path to Private and is there downtime during migration?
[06:05] Jesse: Migration paths exist; most migrations are blue/green with minimal disruption. We'll document migration steps and expected downtime for the planned migration.
[06:12] Elena: A few nuanced asks: 1) We require key rotation policy and ability to rotate customer keys without downtime, 2) we need immutable audit trails > 12 months for some regulators, 3) proof of deletion for specific PII on request. Can you satisfy those?
[06:25] Owen: Key rotation: with CMEK we can plan rotations; typically you can rotate keys in your KMS and we support key aliasing patterns to avoid downtime. Immutable audit trails: for Hosted we can export to your long-term S3/BQ; Dedicated/Private let you manage retention. Proof of deletion: we can provide deletion certificates for covered objects with a documented chain of custody. We'll capture specifics in the follow-up binder.
[06:49] Priya: Also, indemnity and data breach notification timelines — what's your SLA on notifying customers if exfiltration is suspected?
[06:58] Jesse: Our standard is 72-hour notification and we can discuss tighter timelines in the MSA depending on the support tier. We'll flag security incident playbooks in the binder.
[07:07] [noise]
[07:10] Elena: One more — we need to run a short acceptance test: a small scale smoke test to validate that logs, SAML, and KMS integration behave as expected before we go to procurement. Can you support a POC?
[07:20] Jesse: Absolutely — we'll provision a dedicated sandbox with required entitlements. Maya and Owen will own the infra setup; we can run a 2-week POC focusing on token flows, KMS rotate, SAML/SCIM provisioning and log export.
[07:33] Samir: For the POC I'd like to capture metrics: latency 95th at 8k tokens, per-token cost estimates, and audit log delivery times.
[07:41] Maya: We'll include a perf run with sample workload. Note that large contexts affect kernel selection and batching, we'll document the expected throughput.
[07:50] Jesse: Ok let's recap and action items. We'll send SOC2 and ISO attestations, KMS/HSM integration guide, Dedicated vs Private architecture diagram, and a POC setup plan. We'll also share the vendor/subprocessor list and pen test summary under NDA.
[08:05] Elena: Good. Legal will want the retention and deletion language up front. Priya will follow up.
[08:11] Priya: We'll review the binder and come back with an initial redline. Also will need to see the AICPA and ISO cert copies.
[08:18] Jesse: Final Q — any blockers for scheduling the POC the week of Nov 29?
[08:22] Samir: That works for us.
[08:23] Elena: Works for me.
[08:24] Jesse: Great — we'll send the materials tomorrow and set an invite for the POC kickoff. Thanks everyone.

[Post-call notes added by Maya]:
- Deck and artifacts to share: security-deck-v2.pdf, redwood-soc2-2027.pdf (NDA), iso27001-certificate.pdf (NDA), redwood-kms-integration-notes.md, private-deploy-sample.tf
- POC scope: SAML+SCIM provisioning, CMEK key rotation, log export to Venturi S3, perf run (95p latency, token cost)
- Legal ask: retention, deletion proof, subprocessors list, incident notification language

End of transcript.
